tip: Separable verbs put 'ge-' between the prefix and the stem: 'aufräumen' becomes 'aufgeräumt'.
The verb 'empfehlen' puts the person in the dative and the thing in the accusative: 'uns ein hervorragendes Restaurant'.
In the passive, 'von' plus dative names the doer: 'von der Polizei' says who did the catching.
Verbs ending in '-ieren' form the participle without 'ge-': 'reparieren' gives 'repariert', not 'gerepariert'.
In a command a separable prefix moves to the end: 'anrufen' gives 'ruf mich sofort an'.
The 'ihr' command copies the present 'ihr' form without 'ihr': 'setzt euch ... hin'.
When a sentence opens with a non-subject, the verb stays second and the subject follows: 'statt des Autos nehmen wir'.
A plural adjective with no article usually takes the ending '-e': 'rote Rosen'.
Some verbs shift 'e' to 'i' in the 'du' command: 'essen' becomes 'iss'.
The verb 'vorhaben' (to plan) is separable, so 'vor-' splits to the end: 'ich habe vor, ...'.
After 'ein', a neuter adjective usually takes '-es': 'ein dickes Buch'.
Formal reported speech swaps 'ist' for 'sei' to signal you are relaying what someone else said.
With a modal like 'darf' (may), the passive ends in a past participle plus 'werden': 'darf ... genommen werden'.
German often skips the article with an illness: 'Fieber hat', not 'ein Fieber hat'.
'Während' normally takes the genitive: 'während des Urlaubs', not 'dem Urlaub'.
After 'nachdem', the earlier action normally takes the perfect: 'nachdem der Chef eingetroffen ist'.
The verb 'warten' pairs with 'auf' plus the accusative to mean wait for: 'warte auf mich'.
Adjectives usually add '-er' to compare: 'leise' becomes 'leiser', quieter.
The 'du' command of 'sein' is simply 'sei', with no ending: 'sei ehrlich'.
Unlike English 'although', 'obwohl' sends the verb to the very end: 'obwohl es draußen regnet' finishes with 'regnet'.
Informal commands to one person drop the pronoun and the '-st' ending: 'kommen' becomes 'komm'.
Past passive uses 'wurde' plus a participle: 'der Vertrag wurde unterschrieben' marks a completed past action.
Separable verbs slot 'ge-' between prefix and stem in the participle: 'umbauen' becomes 'umgebaut'.
Verbs ending in '-ieren' form the participle with no 'ge-': 'operieren' becomes 'operiert', not 'geoperiert'.
Repeated time points use the accusative: 'jeden Freitag' means every Friday, with 'jeden' marking the case.
Days take 'am', a contraction of 'an dem': 'am Montag' means on Monday.
For a fixed position, 'zwischen' takes the dative: 'zwischen den Stalaktiten' shows location, not movement across.
Comparisons use 'als' for than after a comparative: 'älter als ich' means older than I am.
The verb 'denken' pairs with 'an' plus the accusative to mean think of: 'denk an deinen Regenschirm'.
Verbs that shift 'e' to 'i' keep it in the 'du' command: 'nehmen' gives 'nimm', not 'nehm'.
